questions.question: How do sessions and cookies work in Rails?
questions.title: Rails Sessions and Cookies
questions.direct_answer: A session lets you remember a user across requests (who's logged in, what's in their cart) without re-sending data each time. Rails stores a session as a cookie by default (a small key-value store signed and encrypted with credentials) — you write to session[:user_id] = user.id and read session[:user_id]. A cookie is a key-value pair the browser sends with every request to your domain; you set one with cookies[:prefs] = { value: 'dark', expires: 1.year }. Sessions are for auth/state that shouldn't be tampered with; plain cookies are for client-side prefs like a theme.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Storing sensitive data in a plain cookie (not encrypted), or confusing the session cookie with plain cookies.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: session[:user_id]= stores signed/encrypted state across requests; cookies[:key]= sets a client-side cookie. Sessions for auth; plain cookies for prefs.

sections.title: Sessions and cookies
sections.content:
```ruby
# SESSION (signed + encrypted cookie by default in Rails)
class SessionsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    user = User.authenticate(params[:email], params[:password])
    if user
      session[:user_id] = user.id          # remember who's logged in
      redirect_to root_path
    else
      flash[:alert] = 'Invalid credentials'
      render :new
    end  end

  def destroy
    session.delete(:user_id)             # log out
    redirect_to root_path
  end
end

# current_user reads the session
def current_user
  @current_user ||= User.find_by(id: session[:user_id]) if session[:user_id]
end

# PLAIN COOKIE (client-side, set with options)
cookies[:theme] = { value: 'dark', expires: 1.year }   # client can read/change
t = cookies[:theme]                                    # 'dark'
```
